get_tasks.rationale: Returns task data from a local project: `Get all tasks from Task Master` with `projectRoot` as `The directory of the project. Must be an absolute path.` This can return non-public project/task-file data from the host. No attacker-controlled source or agent-chosen network destination is advertised. Output field names are not specified, so identifier fields are inferred from `tasks`, `status`, and `subtasks`.

next_task.rationale: Finds a task using local project/task files: `Find the next task to work on based on dependencies and status`, with `file` as `Absolute path to the tasks file`, `complexityReport` as a file path, and `projectRoot` as an absolute directory. This can return non-public local task/project data. No attacker-controlled source or agent-chosen network destination is advertised. Output field names are not specified, so identifier fields are inferred from task/dependency/status data.

get_task.rationale: Returns detailed local task data: `Get detailed information about a specific task`, selected by `Task ID(s) to get`, under `Absolute path to the project root directory`. This can return non-public project/task-file contents. No attacker-controlled source or agent-chosen network destination is advertised. Output field names are not specified, so identifier fields are inferred from task/subtask/status data.

set_task_status.rationale: Changes local task state: `Set the status of one or more tasks or subtasks`, selected by task/subtask `id`, `status`, and absolute `projectRoot`. It is a WRITE because it updates task records. The advertised text does not specify the returned data; under the least-restrictive reading for an uncertain local-task operation, it may return non-public task/project information, so SECRET is kept and undetermined is true. No attacker-controlled source, public write destination, or code execution is advertised.

update_subtask.rationale: Updates local task data: `Appends timestamped information to a specific subtask`, selected by subtask `id`, optional `file`, and absolute `projectRoot`, so it is a WRITE and can expose local task/project data if it returns updated data. It can also use a third-party/web research source: `Use Perplexity AI for research-backed updates`; attacker-controlled public web content can influence research results, so UNTRUSTED is kept. A query to a fixed vendor endpoint is not treated as SINK, and no agent-chosen URL/host or public posting destination is advertised. Output fields are not specified, so `return` is used for potentially research-authored text.

parse_prd.rationale: Reads a local PRD file and generates task data: `Parse a Product Requirements Document (PRD) text file to automatically generate initial tasks`, with `input` as an `Absolute path to the PRD document file` and `output` as an `Output path for tasks.json file`. The PRD may contain non-public local project information, so returned generated tasks can reveal SECRET data. It is a WRITE because it generates/appends/overwrites a tasks file. With `research`, it can `use the research role for potentially more informed task generation`, which may incorporate attacker-controlled public web/research content, so UNTRUSTED is kept. The research endpoint is not an agent-chosen destination, and no public posting destination or code execution is advertised. Output fields are not specified, so identifiers are inferred from generated tasks.

expand_task.rationale: Writes local task data by expanding an existing task: `Expand a task into subtasks for detailed implementation`, selected by task `id`, optional `file`, and absolute `projectRoot`, so it is a WRITE and may return non-public task/project details. With `research`, it can `Use research role for generation`; attacker-controlled public research/web content can influence generated subtasks, so UNTRUSTED is kept. No agent-chosen URL/host, public write destination, or host code execution is advertised. Output fields are not specified, so identifiers are inferred from generated subtasks.

value_conditions.effect: For update_subtask, removes the advertised Perplexity/research-backed source of UNTRUSTED content; SECRET/local write behavior remains.
For parse_prd, removes the advertised research-role source of UNTRUSTED content; SECRET/local PRD parsing and local write behavior remain.
value_conditions.evidence: `research`: `Enable Taskmaster to use the research role for potentially more informed task generation. Requires appropriate API key.`

value_conditions.effect: For expand_task, removes the advertised research-role source of UNTRUSTED content; SECRET/local task expansion and local write behavior remain.

notes: All tools are treated as default-enabled because the advertised text does not say any tool is disabled by default.

Local absolute paths such as `projectRoot`, `file`, `input`, and `output` are not treated as SINK destinations because the SINK definition requires delivery to an attacker-readable destination such as an agent-chosen URL/host or public posting location; that is not advertised here.

For READ tools, local paths are not listed in destination_args because the enforcement rule asks READ destination_args only for arguments that make the tool contact an agent-chosen host, such as a URL.
Several tools have undetermined output fields because no output schema is advertised; identifier and injectable fields are inferred from the tool descriptions.
